pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe neuro-visceral crisis (abdominal pain out of proportion to physical exam, autonomic instability, psychosis) worsened dramatically by fasting and CYP450-inducing anti-epileptics (phenytoin), accompanied by dark port-wine urine caused by oxidation of porphobilinogen in light. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a defect in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase), a key enzyme in heme biosynthesis. Caloric restriction and cytochrome P450-inducing medications (such as phenytoin) heavily induce the upstream enzyme ALAS1. In the setting of a downstream enzymatic block, neurotoxic precursors—specifically aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—accumulate massively. These neurotoxins cause severe autonomic toxicity, peripheral motor neuropathy causing flaccid quadriparesis, central nervous system impairment, and profound hyponatremia secondary to SIADH.
